title: SMTPfast vs Resend
description: Two developer-first email APIs compared: pricing per volume, contacts and broadcasts, inbound email, MCP and Terraform support, and where each one actually fits.
introduction:
SMTPfast and Resend answer the same question: how does a developer send email through an API without fighting an enterprise dashboard from 2012? Both are API-first, both have generous free tiers of 3,000 emails a month, and both now ship hosted MCP servers so AI agents can send through them. Every number below is stated plainly so you can verify it against both public pricing pages.

The honest difference is shape. Resend is the larger, more mature product with a bigger ecosystem: official SDKs across many languages, React Email for templates, and SOC 2 compliance messaging aimed at scaling startups. SMTPfast is smaller and priced like it wants your side project and your startup's first two years: contacts, segments and broadcasts are included in every tier rather than sold as a separate marketing product, and the paid tiers undercut Resend at most volumes.

This comparison walks the numbers per volume tier, the feature surface (including the newer agent-facing pieces like hosted MCP servers and Terraform support), and the scenarios where each is the right call.

toolA.name: SMTPfast
toolA.description: A lean email API with transactional sending, inbound receiving, contacts, segments and broadcasts included. Free tier of 3,000 emails/month; paid plans from $9. Ships official SDKs for Node.js, Python, Go and PHP, a Laravel mail driver, a hosted MCP server, an official Terraform provider and an Agent Skill.
pros: Lower price at every paid step: 25,000 emails for $9/month, 100,000 for $19/month, 300,000 for $49/month
Contacts, segments and broadcasts included in every tier, no separate marketing add-on
Hosted newsletter signup forms included, no separate form tool needed
Hosted MCP server with scoped tools plus an official Terraform provider
Free tier includes 3,000 emails/month, 1,000 contacts and broadcasts, no credit card
Gradual sending warm-up for new accounts protects deliverability by default
cons: Free tier is invite-gated: you request access or pay to skip the queue

Official SDKs cover only Node.js, Python, Go and PHP (plus a Laravel mail driver), and they are new (first released in October 2026); other languages call the REST API directly or use a Resend SDK pointed at SMTPfast
Inbound email only on paid plans
Younger product with a smaller community and template ecosystem

toolB.name: Resend
toolB.description: The best-known developer email API of the last few years. React Email templates, SDKs for most languages, inbound email, broadcasts, and a hosted MCP server with a broad tool surface. Free tier of 3,000 emails/month (100/day); Pro from $20.
pros: Mature ecosystem: official SDKs, React Email, extensive docs and examples
Inbound email receiving, not just sending
Hosted MCP server with a broad tool surface and OAuth sign-in for web clients
Instant free tier signup, no invite queue
SOC 2 compliance posture aimed at companies with security review processes
cons: More expensive at volume: Pro is $35 for 100,000 emails, extra emails cost $0.90 per 1,000 once you turn on pay-as-you-go, and Scale starts at $90
Free tier capped at 100 emails/day, which blocks bursty use
Broadcast/audience features grew out of transactional and are priced accordingly at scale

useCases.scenario: A side project or early startup that also needs a newsletter
useCases.explanation: SMTPfast includes contacts, segments and broadcasts in every tier including free, so transactional plus newsletter runs on one bill from day one. Starter covers 10,000 contacts for $9 and Growth 50,000 for $19, where Resend prices marketing contacts separately ($40 a month for 5,000, $250 for 50,000).

useCases.scenario: A product built on React that lives on polished email templates
useCases.explanation: React Email plus Resend's SDKs is the smoothest template workflow in the industry. If your team already thinks in components, nothing else feels as native.

useCases.scenario: High-volume transactional sending on a budget
useCases.explanation: At 100,000 emails a month the gap is $19 versus $35 on Resend Pro. At 200,000 it is $49 versus $125 on Resend Pro with pay-as-you-go turned on, or $160 on Scale. If email volume grows faster than revenue, the pricing curve matters more than ecosystem width.

useCases.scenario: You need to receive email, not just send it
useCases.explanation: Both receive email now: Resend with inbound webhooks, SMTPfast with per-domain receiving on paid plans, a Resend-compatible receiving API and an email.received webhook. If you already integrate Resend receiving, the SMTPfast endpoints and objects have the same shape.

useCases.scenario: AI agents sending email on your behalf
useCases.explanation: Both ship hosted MCP servers, which puts them ahead of nearly every other email provider, and both now cover most of their APIs. SMTPfast keeps API keys and team members out of the agent's reach, and its inboxes let an agent write drafts that a person approves before anything is sent. Pick by how much you want the agent to do on its own.

useCases.scenario: An enterprise security review stands between you and shipping
useCases.explanation: Resend's SOC 2 posture and larger track record clear procurement conversations that a younger product will get stuck in.

faqs.question: Are the free tiers really equivalent?
faqs.answer: Both give 3,000 emails a month, so on volume they are equal. Resend allows 3 domains on its free plan, SMTPfast 1. The tradeoffs differ: Resend caps you at 100 emails a day but signup is instant; SMTPfast has no daily cap and includes 1,000 contacts, hosted signup forms and 2 broadcasts a month, but free access is invite-gated, so you request an invite or start on a paid tier.

faqs.question: Which is cheaper as volume grows?
faqs.answer: SMTPfast at every paid step: $9 for 25k, $19 for 100k, $49 for 300k emails a month. Resend's Pro covers 50k at $20 and 100k at $35, with extra emails at $0.90 per 1,000 if you turn on pay-as-you-go, and Scale is $90 for 100k, $160 for 200k and $350 for 500k. At 50k the difference is $1 ($19 against $20). At 100k it is $19 against $35, about half. At 200k it is $49 against $125 on Pro with pay-as-you-go or $160 on Scale.

faqs.question: Do both work with AI agents over MCP?
faqs.answer: Yes, and both are hosted, so an agent connects with a URL and a credential rather than you running a process. Both now expose a wide surface. SMTPfast has 104 scoped tools covering almost its whole API, with OAuth or an API key; agents cannot create API keys or change team members, which stay with people. Resend also covers templates, broadcasts, domains and API keys, with OAuth for web-based clients.

faqs.question: Can I migrate between them later?
faqs.answer: Sending migrates easily: both are REST APIs with domain verification, so the work is DNS records and swapping the send call. Contacts and suppression lists export and import on both sides. The sticky parts are template ecosystems (React Email on Resend) and any automation built against one MCP server's tool names.

faqs.question: What about deliverability?
faqs.answer: Both manage shared infrastructure reputation and suppression lists. SMTPfast additionally stages sending volume for every new account automatically, lifting limits as the account ages, which protects new senders from burning a domain on day one. Sender reputation still depends mostly on your list hygiene and content, whoever you pick.

faqs.question: How were these numbers sourced?
faqs.answer: Pricing and limits come from both products' public pricing pages, and the MCP details from each provider's documentation, first checked in August 2026 and checked again in October 2026. Where Resend is simply better, the comparison says so: SDK breadth, React Email and compliance posture are Resend wins. If a number has drifted since, both pricing pages are one click away.

decisionMatrix.criteria: Transactional plus newsletter on one bill from day one
Hosted templates with a Templates API
Threaded inboxes with human-approved agent drafts
Official SDK for Ruby, Java, Rust or .NET
Instant free signup for a weekend experiment

verdict.summary: Resend is the safer default for teams that want the biggest ecosystem: official SDKs in more languages, React Email, and a compliance story for security reviews. SMTPfast is the value pick and the simpler one to reason about: contacts and broadcasts included everywhere, inbound email on paid plans with a Resend-compatible receiving API, half the price of Resend Pro at 100k emails a month ($19 against $35), scoped API keys, official SDKs for Node.js, Python, Go and PHP plus a Laravel mail driver, a scoped hosted MCP server, and an official Terraform provider. If you need React Email or a SOC 2 answer, pick Resend. If your bill is driven by volume, or you want transactional, newsletter and inbound in one product without a marketing-tier upsell, SMTPfast costs less at every paid step and does all three.
verdict.recommendation: Choose SMTPfast if your bill is volume-driven, you want transactional plus newsletter plus inbound on one plan, or you want a Terraform-managed setup with scoped keys and agent drafts that a person approves. Choose Resend if you need React Email templates, an official SDK for Ruby, Java, Rust or .NET, or a SOC 2 answer for procurement. Both are REST APIs with hosted MCP servers and compatible receiving endpoints, so switching later is mostly DNS records and a changed base URL.
